one_line_contribution: On a six-template agent benchmark, the experience retriever's value is claimed to be a step function of task-type match — within-type similarity rank (down to rank 50) and removal of near-duplicate bank items do not move task success, while removing the type collapses it — so the retriever can be replaced by a type classifier plus a cached per-type sub-bank, with the only live residual being a compliance hazard that scales with the wrong item's similarity and is content-driven rather than framing-driven.
closest_prior_work: Three verified papers bound this, none of them fatally. (1) Rank-ICL (ICTIR 2026, verified via s2cli channel (a); S2 returns no arXiv id) already reports that ranking-based demonstration selection is only 'competitive with random-shot prompting' — the home-literature statement of rank-flatness. It does not run a within-class rank ladder, has no leave-out ladder, no static baseline, and is on search-result explanation rather than a sequential task, so it bounds the claim's surprise rather than scooping it. (2) arXiv:2411.07130 (MANYICLBENCH, ACL, verified) is the more serious framing threat: it already partitions ICL tasks into 'similar-sample learning' vs 'all-sample learning', i.e. the field already has a name and a metric for tasks where retrieval similarity does not matter and the whole pool works as well as the nearest neighbours. P1 and P6 together amount to placing ALFWorld in the all-sample bucket; the proposal never cites this taxonomy and so overstates how new the question is, though it does test it on trajectories and task success rather than ICL accuracy, which 2411.07130 does not. (3) arXiv:2606.10388 'Right Family, Wrong Skill' (verified, 2026-06-09, SameCapRisk-Bench) is the strongest threat to the harm half: it establishes that a retrieved item from the right family but the wrong specific instance is a distinct and severe failure channel, with harmful-sibling rates rising alongside recall. It measures exposure in a retrieval audit rather than end-task success, and its siblings are within-family whereas P4's wrong items are cross-type, so P4 survives — but 'similarity-scaled harm' is no longer a fresh idea, only a fresh measurement. arXiv:2607.10608 (Compliance Trap, verified) supplies the adoption mechanism the proposal correctly credits.
strongest_objection: The headline contradicts the node's own already-measured number, and the proposal never confronts it. Measurement C reports the best static arm as static3 — three FIXED type-conditioned expert exemplars at ~430 tokens — and k3 − static3 = +17.2 net [+11.9, +22.4], far above the ±8 floor. If the retriever were 'a type classifier plus decoration', a type-conditioned static arm at matched tokens could not lose by +17 net. P1 (rank 50-52 ≈ rank 1-3) and P2 (near-duplicate removal is inert) jointly assert that within-type item identity does not matter; combined with the measured +17.2 they are close to a contradiction, because the only remaining difference between k3 and static3 is which within-type items appear and that they vary per game. Either P1/P2 will be falsified, or the true operative variable is per-episode item variety rather than similarity — an interesting result, but one the proposal neither predicts nor names an interpretation for. Tellingly, the 'random-within-type at matched length' cell, which is the single most informative arm in the whole design for exactly this question, is listed as a baseline and carries no pre-registered prediction at all. The Risk Factors section anticipates the opposite worry (that the residual might be inside the floor) and so reads as written before Measurement C landed. Secondary damage: the entailment check's two flags are real and unfixed. P3's falsifier cannot fire because L3 is definitionally the same construction as P4's most-similar-wrong-type arm, so P4's asserted harm protects P3's null from below and the one-sided test is unfalsifiable under the proposal's own mechanism; P7's falsifier requires whole-bank similarity to return wrong-type items, which ALFWorld's type-diagnostic goal sentences make near-impossible, and the wrong-type return rate is not even among the logged secondary metrics, so the null is fixed by bge-m3 rather than tested. P2 is not independent of P1 (L2's retrieval from the remainder is the rank ladder renamed), and P6's cost clause is true by construction. That leaves P4 and P5 as the only genuinely independent two-sided tests, and P4 confounds similarity with delivery (three retrieved items vs Measurement C's single fixed exemplar, with no token matching stated for the placebo — a direct violation of the brief's own binding 'token- and rate-matched placebos' rule).
what_would_fix_it: (1) State P1/P2 against the measured +17.2 residual, as the brief's binding rule requires, and add the decomposition the design already has the cells for: promote 'random-within-type at matched length' to the headline prediction, since random-within-type ≈ rank 1-3 while static3 sits 17 net below would identify per-episode item variety, not similarity, as the retriever's real function — a positive, publishable claim instead of a null. Pre-register both outcomes and their interpretations. (2) Fix P3 by making the falsifier two-sided and adding a random-wrong-type RETRIEVED cell matched to L3 in selection rule and item count, so L3 is compared like-for-like rather than against a single fixed exemplar. (3) Fix P7 by reporting the type-agnostic arm's wrong-type return rate as a gating manipulation check and adding a degraded-key variant (type verb masked, or an object-only key) so a nonzero wrong-type rate exists for the prediction to be about; if the rate is zero, withdraw P7 rather than report it as a confirmed null. (4) Token-match the wrong-type placebo to the similar-wrong arm (three wrong items, not one) so P4 varies similarity alone. (5) Declare a multiplicity policy: five of seven predictions are equivalence claims at ±8 with a CI half-width of ~±5 across 16 cells, and with no correction at least one spurious null is expected. (6) Run the rank and leave-out ladders on the self pool (1,892 on-policy successes, already on disk) as well as the expert pool — rank-flatness on a curated six-template expert bank is much weaker evidence than rank-flatness on a noisy on-policy bank, and it costs no new infrastructure.
missing_baseline: A within-type but degraded-content arm: top-3 items of the correct type drawn from failed trajectories, or correct-type items with the action sequence corrupted or truncated, at matched length. Every arm in the plan that destroys content also destroys type (the wrong-type placebo, L3), so the design cannot separate 'the reader needs the type's correct procedure' from 'the reader needs any plausibly formatted action sequence of the right type'. That distinction is the paper's central interpretive claim and P1/P2's flatness is exactly what makes it urgent: if rank 50 works as well as rank 1, the natural next question is whether a wrong-but-well-formed within-type trajectory works too, and nothing in the 16 cells answers it. Second omission: a token- and item-count-matched random wrong-type RETRIEVED placebo (three items) for P3 and P4, rather than Measurement C's single fixed exemplar.
